baseline_comparison.fairness_caveat: The path baseline ranks a bounded, per-disease discovered candidate set (0-500 candidates depending on the disease). Popularity and TransE both rank the complete, fixed 7,957-drug universe for every disease. All three share the same held-out pairs and the same filtered-rank/Hits@K/MRR formulas, but they are not the same task -- no "N times better/worse" comparison between path and {popularity, TransE} should be made without this caveat attached every time the numbers are shown together.

interpretation.summary: Final TransE did not outperform the existing path baseline on the locked test, and scored only modestly above -- or broadly near -- the simple non-learning baselines on several ranking metrics (e.g. TransE MRR 0.0100 vs. popularity MRR_approx 0.0062 vs. path MRR 0.033294).
interpretation.motivates: testing a relation-aware GNN (e.g. R-GCN) next, since a pure translational embedding model may be under-using PrimeKG's relational structure that the path baseline (which reasons over typed multi-hop paths) and a relational GNN can both exploit more directly.

protocol_notes.locked_test_must_not_be_used_for_iterati: This locked test has now been observed once, by design, and must not be reused as an iterative tuning or model-selection set for any future model (including R-GCN). A future model must be selected using training/validation splits only; any future final comparison against this TransE result must use a precommitted protocol and avoid any test-driven changes.
